ai.description: *Hemidactylus imbricatus* reaches 10 cm. It features a patterned brown body with a thickened, carrot-shaped tail and granular scales. It lacks toe pads, distinguishing it from other geckos.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus imbricatus* is uniquely identified by its distinctively swollen, carrot-shaped tail, which lacks the prominent, elongated tubercles found on other Indian geckos.
ai.habitat: The Carrot-tail Viper Gecko inhabits arid, rocky scrublands and dry deciduous forests in India, typically found sheltering under stones or in rock crevices.
ai.behavior: The Carrot-tail Viper Gecko is primarily nocturnal and utilizes a unique defensive display by arching its back and vibrating its carrot-shaped tail to mimic a venomous snake.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus imbricatus* is oviparous, typically laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus imbricatus* is found in arid regions of Pakistan and northwestern India, specifically across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and parts of Haryana and Punjab.
